# One payload rule per channel codec, and the same rule in every SDK whose
# channels carry no type.
#
# `entry|sink|payload|expected`, one case per line. `entry` and `sink` name the
# codec each end of a channel declares, or `none` when it names no codec. The
# payload is decoded by the entry, the value it yields is encoded by the sink,
# and `expected` is the bytes that encoding sends, or `decode_error` or
# `encode_error` when that step refuses.
#
# `<empty>` is no bytes, and `hex:` spells bytes that are not text. A case that
# names `msgpack` is read only by the SDKs that ship MessagePack.
#
# The cases are what every one of these SDKs sends alike. Where the rule lets
# them differ, each SDK's own test says so: a Ruby or PHP string is its bytes, so
# it passes a `bytes` sink, and a Python or Node string does not.
#
# Every SDK's own suite feeds this file to the slots its builder resolves:
#   sdk/ruby/test/authoring_test.rb       Ruby
#   sdk/python/tests/test_authoring.py    Python
#   sdk/node/test/authoring.test.mjs      Node
#   sdk/php/tests/AuthoringTest.php       PHP

text|none|hello|hello
text|text|hello|hello
text|json|hi|"hi"
text|json|héllo|"héllo"
text|none|hex:ff|decode_error
none|none|{"a":1}|{"a":1}
none|json|{"a":1}|{"a":1}
none|none|[1,2]|[1,2]
none|none|42|42
none|none|1.5|1.5
none|none|true|true
none|none|<empty>|null
none|none|"hi"|hi
none|none|"é"|é
none|json|"hi"|"hi"
none|none|hello|decode_error
none|text|42|encode_error
none|bytes|42|encode_error
json|json|"hi"|"hi"
bytes|none|hex:ff00|hex:ff00
bytes|bytes|hex:ff00|hex:ff00
bytes|text|hex:ff|encode_error
none|msgpack|42|hex:2a
msgpack|none|hex:a26869|hi
msgpack|text|hex:a26869|hi
msgpack|none|hex:81a16101|{"a":1}
